name: user_context
title: What the user is looking at
description: What the user is working on right now in Forge: the file and line they are on and what they selected, the files they have open, the problems the language servers report near their cursor, the end of the terminal they last used, and the tests that failed in their last run. Call it when they refer to "this", "here", "the error" or "the failing test".

name: remember
title: Remember for the project
description: Propose a note for the project's standing instructions (its AGENTS.md), which agents get at the start of every session: how to build or test it, a convention, a trap you ran into. One short, self-contained note per call. The user may edit it, and keeps it or not; returns which.

note.description: The note, in a sentence or two, as an instruction.

name: ask_user
title: Ask the user
description: Ask the user a question in the conversation and wait for the answer, instead of ending your turn to ask. Give `options` when the answer is one of a few choices (the user clicks one, or writes something else). Returns the answer, or that the user skipped the question (then decide yourself and say what you chose).

name: notify
title: Notify the user
description: Tell the user something worth their attention now (a long task finished, something needs them) with a notification in Forge. Doesn't wait for anything.

name: propose_commit
title: Propose a commit
description: Propose a git commit to the user instead of running `git commit`. Forge shows the message and the files in the conversation; the user commits them from Forge, edits the message in the Git panel, or declines. Waits for that decision and returns the new commit's SHA and final message, or that the user declined. Don't stage files yourself: list them in `files`. Don't write Signed-off-by lines: Forge signs the commit off as the user when the repository asks for it.

message.description: The commit message: a subject line, then optionally a blank line and a body. Follow the repository's style.

files.description: Files to commit, relative to the project root (or absolute). Leave it out to commit every change.

name: propose_push
title: Propose a push
description: Propose pushing the current branch to the user instead of running `git push`. Forge shows the branch, where it goes and the commits it takes; the user pushes or declines. Pushes go to the branch's upstream, or create the branch on the remote and make it the upstream. Never forced. Waits for that decision and returns the result.

remote.description: The remote to push to. Leave it out for the branch's upstream (or `origin` for a new branch).

name: diagnostics
title: Errors and warnings
description: The errors and warnings the language servers report, as the user sees them in the editor (unsaved edits included): in a file or a folder, in the files you changed in this conversation, or in every file that has some. Waits for the servers to catch up after recent edits. Faster than building the project.

path.description: Only this file, or the files in this folder (relative to the project root).

severity.description: Only errors, or only warnings. Leave it out for both.

changed.description: Only the files you changed in this conversation.

name: check_file
title: Check your changes
description: After editing: the problems your changes brought to a file (or to every file you changed in this conversation), once the language servers have looked at the new code. Problems the file already had before you changed it are left out (only counted), so what it lists is yours to fix. Call it after each round of edits, before moving on.

path.description: The file (relative to the project root). Leave it out for every file you changed.

name: go_to_definition
title: Go to definition
description: Where a symbol is defined, according to the language server: file, line, column and that line's code.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

line.description: The line the symbol is on (1-based).

symbol.description: The symbol's name, as written on that line.

name: find_references
title: Find references
description: Every place a symbol is used, according to the language server (more precise than text search): file, line, column and code.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

line.description: The line the symbol is on (1-based).

symbol.description: The symbol's name, as written on that line.

name: rename_symbol
title: Rename a symbol
description: Rename a symbol everywhere it is used, with the language server's rename (like the editor's), instead of search and replace. The change goes through the editor and into the conversation's changes, which the user reviews; the user may be asked first. Returns the files changed.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

line.description: The line the symbol is on (1-based).

symbol.description: The symbol's name, as written on that line.

name: hover
title: Type and docs
description: What the language server says about a symbol: its type or signature and its documentation.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

line.description: The line the symbol is on (1-based).

symbol.description: The symbol's name, as written on that line.

name: document_symbols
title: File outline
description: A file's outline from its language server: its types, functions, methods and fields, nested, with their lines. Read it before reading a large file whole, to go straight to the part you need.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

name: go_to_implementation
title: Go to implementations
description: Where an interface, a trait or an abstract/virtual method is implemented, according to the language server.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

line.description: The line the symbol is on (1-based).

symbol.description: The symbol's name, as written on that line.

name: go_to_type_definition
title: Go to type definition
description: Where the type of a variable, parameter or expression is defined (not the variable itself).

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

line.description: The line the symbol is on (1-based).

symbol.description: The symbol's name, as written on that line.

name: call_hierarchy
title: Call hierarchy
description: Who calls a function or method (`incoming`, the default), or what it calls (`outgoing`), with where: to see what a change to it affects before making it.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

line.description: The line the function's name is on (1-based).

symbol.description: The function's name, as written on that line.

name: signature_help
title: Signature help
description: The signatures (overloads) and parameter docs of the function called on a line, as `symbol(…)`: what to pass it.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

line.description: The line the symbol is on (1-based).

symbol.description: The symbol's name, as written on that line.

name: workspace_symbols
title: Find symbols
description: Types, functions and other symbols whose name matches, across the project, with where they are (the language servers' workspace symbols).

query.description: A name or part of it.

name: code_actions
title: Code actions
description: The language server's code actions on some lines: quick fixes for the problems there, imports to add, refactors. Apply one with `apply_code_action`.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

line.description: First line (1-based); for a problem's fix, its line.

end_line.description: Last line, when more than one.

name: apply_code_action
title: Apply a code action
description: Apply one of the code actions `code_actions` listed for those lines, by its exact title. The change goes through the editor into the conversation's changes; the user may be asked first. Returns the files changed.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

line.description: First line (1-based); for a problem's fix, its line.

end_line.description: Last line, when more than one.

title.description: The action's exact title, as `code_actions` listed it.

name: format_file
title: Format a file
description: Format a file with the project's formatter (as the editor's Format does). The change joins the conversation's changes.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

name: set_breakpoint
title: Set a breakpoint
description: Set a breakpoint at a line (replacing one already there), optionally only when a condition holds. It shows in the editor's gutter; running debug sessions pick it up. Returns the breakpoints set.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

condition.description: Stop only when this expression (in the program's language) is true.

name: remove_breakpoint
title: Remove a breakpoint
description: Remove the breakpoint at a line, or every breakpoint with `all`.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

name: start_debugging
title: Start debugging
description: Debug a run target (like the title bar's Debug) or tests (like a test's Debug button), with the breakpoints set. Builds, starts, and waits until it stops at a breakpoint: returns where (stack) and the local variables, or that it ended without stopping. Tests are waited for up to a minute; an app for 15 seconds, since a server stops only once something calls it: then trigger that code (`http_request` returns where the program stops). Give `test_path` or `test_name` for tests, else `target` (or nothing, for the selected target).

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for it to stop (default: 60 for tests, 15 for an app).

test_path.description: Debug the tests in this file or folder.

test_name.description: Debug the tests whose name contains this.

name: debug_step
title: Continue or step
description: Move the paused program on and wait until it stops again: `continue` (to the next breakpoint), `step_over`, `step_in`, `step_out`, or `pause` a running program. Returns the new stack and local variables, or that it ended.

name: debug_evaluate
title: Evaluate an expression
description: Evaluate an expression in the paused program's current frame (as the debug console does) and return its value and type.

name: stop_debugging
title: Stop debugging
description: End the debug session.

name: show_file
title: Show a file to the user
description: Open a file in the user's editor at a line (or a range of lines, selected), to point them at something you are talking about.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

end_line.description: Last line of the range to select.

name: show_changes
title: Show your changes
description: Open the review of the files you changed in this conversation as diffs (where the user keeps or undoes each change), at one file if given.

path.description: The file to show first.

name: read_file
title: Read a file
description: Reads lines of a file, numbered, as Forge has it (unsaved edits included): from `start_line`, or the last `tail` lines. Use it instead of `head`, `tail`, `sed -n` or `cat` in a shell. Without `lines` it reads 250 lines.

path.description: The file, relative to the project root (or absolute).

tail.description: Read the last this many lines instead.

name: search
title: Search the project
description: Searches the project's files for text or a regex with Forge's search (the Search panel's): unsaved edits included, files git ignores and the ones kept from agents left out. Answers `path:line: text` like grep. Use it instead of `grep`, `rg` or `find` in a shell.

query.description: The text to find, or a regex when `regex` is true.

include.description: Only files matching these globs (comma-separated or a list), e.g. `*.rs` or `src/**`.

exclude.description: Leave out files matching these globs.

files_only.description: List only the matching files, with how many lines match.

max_results.description: Stop after this many matching lines (default 100).

name: git_history
title: Search git history
description: Reads the repository's history, without changing anything. `action`: `log` (commits, of `path` if given, following renames; filter by `author`, `since`, `message`), `changes` (commits that added or removed `text`, or whose changed lines match `regex`; `patch` for their diffs), `show` (a `commit`: message and diff, of `path` if given; `stat_only` for the files), `file_at` (`path` as it was at `commit`), `blame` (who last changed each line of `path`, `start_line`-`end_line`), `diff` (between `from` and `to`, or `from` and the working tree, or the uncommitted changes; `stat_only` for the files). Use it instead of git commands in a shell.

path.description: A file or folder, relative to the project root.

regex.description: `changes`: a regex the changed lines match (git log -G).

stat.description: `log`: list the files each commit changed.

stat_only.description: `show`/`diff`: only the files and their changed line counts.

to.description: `diff`: the commit to compare to (default: the working tree).

name: run_command
title: Run a command
description: Runs a shell command in a terminal of Forge's that the user watches live in this conversation, and returns its exit code and output (the end of it, if long) once it ends. Use it for builds, installs, scripts, migrations and anything that takes a while (your own shell tool only shows the user the output at the end). The user's permission settings apply, as for your other commands.

command.description: The command line, run by the user's shell.

cwd.description: Where to run it, relative to the project root (default: the root).

tail.description: Pass on only the last this many lines of the output (instead of `| tail`).

head.description: Pass on only the first this many lines of the output (instead of `| head`).

filter.description: Pass on only the output lines matching this regex (instead of `| grep`); with `tail` or `head`, of those.

name: forge_settings
title: Forge's settings
description: Looks up Forge's settings (the editor's, the terminal's, git, languages, .NET, agents, each extension's…), as the Settings tab has them: each one's key, description, type or allowed values, default and current value, and the file it is in. Search by words (`font size terminal`), or list a whole page with `page`. Use it before proposing changes with `change_settings`.

query.description: Words that the setting's key, title or description contain.

page.description: Only this page (its id, as results show it).

name: change_settings
title: Change settings
description: Proposes changes to Forge's settings: the user sees each one (before → after) and applies or discards them. They take effect at once. `key` as `forge_settings` shows it; `value: null` puts the default back. Agents' own setup (which agents run, their permissions and MCP servers) is the user's to change: don't propose it.

value.description: The new value, of the setting's type; null for the default.

page.description: The page, when the key is on several.

name: forge_keybindings
title: Key bindings
description: What keys do in Forge (and in which context), or which keys run an action: give `keys` (`cmd-shift-p`, `cmd-k cmd-t`; `secondary` is cmd on macOS and ctrl elsewhere) or words of an action's name (`action`: `minimap`, `terminal::Toggle`). Actions without keys are listed too.

name: change_keybinding
title: Change a key binding
description: Proposes a key binding for the user's keymap.json: `keys` run `action` (with `args`, if it takes any) where `context` holds (`Editor`, `Workspace`, `Terminal`; everywhere when left out), or do nothing there with `action: null`. The user applies or discards it; it takes effect at once.

action.description: The action's name, as `forge_keybindings` shows it; null to unbind.

args.description: The action's arguments, for actions that take some.

name: forge_guide
title: Forge's guide
description: Forge's own documentation: how its features work and where they are set up (agents, threads, tests, debugging, git, .NET, HTTP files, extensions…). Without `topic`, its sections; with one, the sections about it.
